summary: The note describes the Kelly Cup, the trophy awarded to the playoff champion of the ECHL since 1997. It explains that the cup replaced the earlier Riley Cup, names the league figure it honors, and outlines how the trophy is loaned and replaced. It also mentions the playoff MVP award given during the championship ceremonies.
one_line: The Kelly Cup is the ECHL playoff championship trophy, awarded since 1997 and named after league commissioner Patrick J. Kelly.
key_facts: The Patrick J. Kelly Cup goes to the playoff champion of the ECHL.
The Kelly Cup has been awarded to teams since 1997.
Prior to 1997, the playoff winner was awarded the Riley Cup.
The Riley Cup was named after former American Hockey League president Jack Riley.
The current cup is named after Patrick J. Kelly, the league's first commissioner.
The cup is loaned to the winning team for one year.
The cup is returned at the start of the following year's playoffs.
The trophy itself has been replaced three times.
The first two iterations of the trophy are preserved in the Hockey Hall of Fame.
The Kelly Cup Playoffs Most Valuable Player award is given out as part of the Kelly Cup Championship ceremonies.
Nick Vitucci and Dave Gagnon are the only players to win the Kelly Cup Playoffs MVP award on multiple occasions.
